summary: Dashboard variable evaluation order flips under live-filter edits, dropping route-anchored alert context
description:
Issue summary:
Customers report that when editing live dashboard filters (variable-driven panels), the variable evaluation order briefly flips, causing alerts that are scoped to a specific route_tag to lose their route context. This shows up as alert notifications without the expected route_id/tracing parameters and dashboard snapshots that no longer link to trace hooks for the affected route.

Impact:
- BrightWave seeing missed alert context for three production dashboards. Several on-call pages arrived without route identifiers, delaying incident triage.
- Affects enterprise customers who rely on route-anchored alert links for fast debugging.
- Intermittent: appears when users rapidly toggle or edit multiple dashboard variables in sequence; reproduces ~7/10 in customer environment.

Environment:
- Console web (React) + backend query-engine (prod us-east).
- Customer org: BrightWave Analytics (enterprise).
- Dashboards use dynamic variables: $org_route, $service_env, $time_window. Alerts bound to panel use route hook (tracehook) tokens generated at snapshot time.

Steps to reproduce (observed by customer):
1) Open dashboard A (route-scoped alert attached to panel).
2) Edit filter $service_env from "staging" to "prod" then immediately change $org_route via type-ahead.
3) Save or run query quickly; trigger snapshot/alert evaluation.
4) Observe that the alert notification (Slack/Email) is missing route_id and tracehook parameters; dashboard snapshot loses trace link.

Logs / traces collected:
- Console logs from customer session showing variable change events batching: variable-change events: [env->prod, route->r-42] arrived out of order at backend aggregator.
- Query-engine trace (trace-id: 2f9b-0a7c) shows two distinct evaluation passes: preliminary evaluation that produced cached route context, then a second pass that applied variables in reversed order and dropped the route tag before alert rendering.
- No 5xx or rate-limit errors.

Initial customer request:
Customer asked for: (1) root cause and mitigation to ensure alert notifications preserve route context, (2) a short-term workaround they can apply to dashboards/alerts to avoid missing trace hooks.

Notes on urgency:
Assigned P1 / Sev1 because enterprise on-call tooling degraded and manual triage was required for at least one production page.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:15 - Priya Menon (Support): Logged initial report from BrightWave. Attached customer screenshots, console logs, and a short screen recording showing rapid edits. Assigned to on-call Console eng.

2026-03-10 11:02 - Liam O'Connor (Console Eng): Confirmed reproducible in a local staging copy when toggling variables quickly. Hypothesis: frontend change-batching is not preserving intended evaluation order when updates are collapsed into the same micro-batch, and backend query-engine treats the last-writer-first in some cache merge path.

2026-03-10 13:40 - SRE (Maya Chen): Captured backend trace-id 2f9b-0a7c and verified no downstream failures. Observed two evaluation passes in short succession. Suggested checking the variable-eval optimizer and the alert-eval hook that composes tracehook tokens after variable resolution.

2026-03-11 09:12 - Liam O'Connor: Added unit test reproducer for variable-event collision. Pushing a small change to ensure strict ordering of variable-change events before running alert-eval path: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2438

2026-03-12 08:55 - Priya Menon (Support): Customer confirmed a temporary mitigation: adding a short debounce (400ms) on manual dashboard variable edits stops the mis-eval in their environment. They asked for a server-side fix so their users don't have to change UX behavior.
investigation_notes: Reproducer built in staging. Root cause: frontend batches variable-change events into a "collapsed update" with nondeterministic ordering when multiple edits happen within the microtask window. The backend query-engine merge logic assumes deterministic precedence of variable values in the batch; in a rare code path it applied the last-applied variable but then composed alert tracehook using an earlier evaluation context (race between cache write and alert token generation). Race happens ~10-30ms window. The issue surfaced after a recent optimization that tried to reduce evaluation passes by coalescing variable updates (deploy 2026-02-28).
resolution_notes:
Work in progress: two parallel fixes planned:
1) Frontend: make variable-change batching preserve event order deterministically and add a 50ms micro-debounce to reduce reordering without degrading UX.
2) Backend: make alert-eval tracehook generation atomic with variable-resolution snapshot (ensure token composition uses the same variable state as the evaluation that triggered the alert).

Temporary workaround provided to customer: add a dashboard-level 400ms debounce on variable edits (they applied via custom embedded dashboard wrapper).

PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2438 (frontend ordering), https://github.com/redwood-inference/query-engine/pull/987 (backend atomic tracehook snapshot)

Planned rollout: frontend hotfix to staging for validation 2026-03-13, backend fix to staging same day. Coordinate canary release to prod-us-east 2026-03-15 with monitoring on alert-link completeness metric.
